sourceRefs.locator: Historic excavation photograph CfO0176, C55000/1, 1904. Norwegian caption identifies foreman Aksel Stubstad, engineers Glende and Beck, and preparator Paul Johannesen. File record credits Olaf Væring and documents CC BY-SA 4.0.
Collegium Medievale 29, pp. 84–87, “Oseberggravningen”; fig. 2 and pp. 84–85 on five bark-edge samples, the two posts and ridge, the pressure-deformed chamber, and drawings by Glende and Beck.
Opening account of Oskar Rom’s visit to Gustafson in August 1903; “An archaeological adventure” and “Important events” for the main excavation in June 1904.

“What do the motifs on the Oseberg tapestry signify?”, “Exotic goods from Persia and Byzantium” and “The colours that disappeared”; clothing strips, the reversed silk, tools and Sofie Krafft’s 41 drawings of 110 silk pieces.
